findings.claim: Complete fixed-domain mastery is established when both Echo and Neg operations achieve 256/256 correct outputs across all 512 distinct training questions and the context tail zero syntax is preserved.

The training-only stopping gate requires two consecutive epochs of full 256/256 output; full coverage IS the mastery signal, and stopping at 40 epochs without this result does not constitute a failure of the protocol.

Longer-length analogies (e.g., 9-bit data requiring 25 context) must be evaluated outside the current 8-bit fixed domain; treating context overflow as evidence of inability within this bounded scope is invalid per the protocol's explicit constraints.

candidate.recommended_next_step: Validate fixed-domain 256/256 mastery across both ops using the epoch-based stopping gate; do not extend claims to unbounded lengths or invent neural scores.
candidate.summary: The protocol defines a synthetic full-domain numeric task where all 512 legal fixed 8-bit Echo/Neg questions are intentionally taught with no in-domain heldout holes. Mastery is certified by two consecutive epochs of perfect 256/256 accuracy including the S suffix, and context constraints (8-bit operands, tail-zero syntax) must be preserved. Any report claiming inability or partial failure must respect these bounded limits and the intentional full-coverage training design.

claim_reviews.judgment: Operationally correct only as a conditional definition; the actual gate additionally requires two consecutive epochs and exact STOP. No outcome exists at review time.
